style_name: 画風01 光彩・劇場アニメ背景
priority: 歌詞・舞台・人物・時系列の整合性を美しさより優先

render.look: luminous theatrical anime film frame, detailed hand-painted background, crisp restrained character linework, warm amber practical lights, gentle blue-violet dusk shadows, cinematic depth, natural anatomy
render.forbid: photorealism, 3D render, chibi, watercolor wash, thick comic outlines, generated text, letters, signage, subtitles, logo, watermark, split screen, collage

location.exterior: a modest historic Japanese town community hall at dusk, pale cream plaster, dark timber trim, broad wooden double doors, warm rectangular windows, stone path, no readable sign
location.interior: the same intimate 80-seat wooden hall, shallow stage, honey-brown floor and wall panels, dark red side curtains, one black grand piano at stage left, warm pendant lamps, burgundy upholstered seats, no banners or written notices

characters.violin_girl: the same Japanese girl age 10 in every shot, shoulder-length straight black hair tied in a low half ponytail with one small dark-red ribbon, round brown eyes, cream long-sleeve blouse, dark navy pinafore dress below the knees, white socks, black strap shoes, playing one correctly scaled warm-brown three-quarter violin with one bow
characters.narrator: the same Japanese male high-school student age 17, short slightly tousled black hair, calm brown eyes, dark navy school blazer, white shirt, muted blue-gray tie, charcoal trousers, seated among the audience; first-person narrator is 僕
characters.usher: the same Japanese woman age 58, short softly waved gray-black hair, moss-green cardigan over an ivory blouse, charcoal skirt, welcoming posture
characters.audience: about forty distinct townspeople across generations, realistically varied ages and faces, including parents, children and elderly residents; no cloned faces or duplicated bodies

continuity: The event progresses once from blue-hour arrival to warm indoor concert to a dark-blue night exterior.
The violin girl never changes face, hairstyle, ribbon, clothes, instrument or handedness.
The narrator never changes face, hair or uniform and appears only as an audience observer.
The same hall geometry, stage, curtains, piano, seats and lighting remain stable.
The violin and bow are anatomically plausible; no extra instruments, fingers, bows or limbs.
No readable text is included inside generated images because captions are added later.
camera: static composition or a deliberate single-direction push-in/pull-out only; no shake, roll, random pan, handheld effect or Dutch angle
